notes:
Recorded under the owner's v0.17 assurance-closure mandate of 2026-09-07, priority 1: register mcp-re-policy's actual authority/authorities, measure existing evidence, eliminate only genuine duplicated mappings, and add subordinate theorems only where a meaningful security proposition exists. Recorded by the implementing agent as routine owner-review maintenance, not as a transcription of a ruling naming this fingerprint. The measurement record is verification/reviews/packets/policy-authority-2026-09-07.md.

THE RULING WAS FOLLOWED AS AN AUDIT, NOT A UNIFICATION. PolicyError, AuthorizationRefusal and RefusalCause are three semantic authorities and stay three. What the audit measured is that the delegation chain was ALREADY correct: PdpRelationRefusal::wire_code returns a PolicyError VARIANT rather than a string, AuthorizationRefusal asks each arm, and RefusalCause composes without reading either vocabulary. No layer reproduces the PolicyError -> mcp-re.authorization_* table and none acquired a PolicyError -> McpReError projection. One wording correction was needed: RefusalCause::wire_code called itself 'the ONLY rendering point', which reads as a claim to own the subordinate mapping. It composes; the wording now says so.

THREE OF SIX POLICY FILES HAD NO CONSUMER AND WERE A SECOND AUTHORITY. block.rs (the params._meta sibling-block parser, already named a legacy input in docs/architecture/authorization.md section 2.5), decision.rs (Allow | Deny(PolicyError), strictly weaker than the ADR-MCPRE-065 posture types that THM-0056 and THM-0046 are about) and wire.rs (an UNSIGNED JSON-RPC denial envelope, carrying open finding #144) each had zero consumers anywhere in the tree. Deleted; the crate now depends on thiserror and nothing else. revocation.rs is retained and deliberately NOT in the registered unit: LiveTrustResolver's seam is allow(dead_code) and documents itself NOT WIRED, so it is excluded on the precedent that kept trust_plane/window_policy.rs and async_replay/l1_fast_reject.rs out of their units. Never state a theorem over dormant code.

THE FINDING THE AUDIT WAS NOT LOOKING FOR: A FIFTH MINTING PRODUCER. ADR-MCPRE-066 Slice 2 established that one file decides what an mcp-re.* token says, enforced over a hand-maintained list of four producer files — the shape section 2.1 of that ADR names as its own defect, and #637 had already found a fourth it had never been told about. There was a fifth: mcp-re-client-core/src/binding_spec/refusal.rs matched BindingSpecRefusal onto two &'static str literals, and BOTH published SDKs render refusals through it via build_authorization. A token renamed in Core would have left two shipped surfaces emitting the old spelling with nothing able to notice. Fixed the way Slice 2 fixed the other four: an exhaustive From<&BindingSpecRefusal> for McpReError with no wildcard arm, wire_code derived from it. Negative-controlled: re-introducing a literal fails the guard.

THE LIST WAS REPLACED BY A MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS WHAT THIS THEOREM IS. Adding the fifth file to the list would have repeated the mistake. exactly_two_files_decide_what_a_verdict_token_says walks EVERY workspace crate's source tree and asserts the set of files holding a verdict-token literal is exactly {mcp-re-core/src/error.rs, mcp-re-policy/src/error.rs}; the_scanned_crate_set_is_the_workspace derives the crate list from the workspace Cargo.toml at compile time, so a new member is scanned or the lane fails. A verdict token is mcp-re.<name> with no further dot; the dotted spellings are audit event types, whose sets three existing controls pin exactly.

THE PRIMITIVE THE WALK RESTS ON WAS BROKEN, AND THAT IS PART OF THIS RECORD. mcp_re_test_paths::rust_source::production_half blanked ordinary string literals per line, knew nothing of raw strings, and forgot its state at every newline. mcp-re-client-core/src/execution_contract.rs writes a raw byte string holding JSON across five lines inside a cfg(test) module; the unbalanced braces closed the region three lines early and TWENTY-SEVEN LINES OF TEST CODE were measured as production by every guard built on the primitive. It is now a stateful lexer (rust_source/brace_scan.rs) covering ordinary strings, raw strings with their hash count, character literals, lifetimes, line comments and nested block comments, with five regression tests; scripts/module_size_gate.py carries the same scanner so the two cannot drift. MEASURED IMPACT: 622 tracked .rs files, ONE changed count, downward, and no registered file grew — the module-size ratchet is unaffected.

TWO FILES CROSSED THE THRESHOLD AND WERE DECOMPOSED ALONG REAL SEAMS, NOT TO SATISFY A NUMBER. rust_source.rs held two authorities — which characters are code, and where a test region begins and ends — and the lexer moved out; that is the invalidation boundary too. source_fallbacks.rs mixed where a guard's input lives with which test witnesses a claim, and the witness map moved to traceability_sources.rs: a relocation and a re-evidencing are not the same event.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. Not that the projections' GROUPINGS are right — which carrier failure is which Core verdict is the ratified MCPRE-92 owner decision and no guard can see a wrong mapping. Not that the two token sets are disjoint: mcp-re.authorization_binding_profile_required is spelled by both with different meanings, separated on the wire by data.policy, and the Core spelling has no production producer on this tree — left as measured because the tokens are frozen and re-spelling one is an ADR, not something an ownership audit decides. Not the correctness of either taxonomy, and not that a refusal reaches the audit boundary, which is THM-0046's, THM-0069's and THM-0071's. Scoped to the Cargo/Bazel workspace: sdk/python and sdk/typescript are separate Cargo workspaces with no Bazel target, and are covered by the producer check on the file they render through.
